verses.1:1: In the land of Uz there was a man—Job was his name—and that man was blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil.
verses.1:2: To him were born seven sons and three daughters.
verses.1:3: His livestock amounted to seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yokes of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys, along with a very large household of servants; so that man was greater than all the sons of the east.
verses.1:4: Now his sons would go and prepare a banquet at each one's house on his own day, and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
verses.1:5: When the days of the banquet had completed their cycle, Job would send and sanctify them, and he would rise early in the morning and offer up burnt offerings matching the number of them all; for Job said, "Maybe my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." In this way Job would do continually.
verses.1:6: Now the day arrived when the sons of God came to take their stand before the LORD, and Satan came in their midst as well.
verses.1:7: And the LORD said to Satan, "Where are you coming from?" Satan answered the LORD and said, "From ranging across the earth and from walking back and forth on it."
verses.1:8: Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you turned your thoughts to My servant Job? For there is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning aside from evil."
verses.1:9: Satan answered the LORD and said, "Is it for nothing that Job fears God?
verses.1:10: Have You not hedged around him and around his house and around all that belongs to him on every side? The work of his hands You have blessed, and his livestock have burst forth across the land.
verses.1:11: Yet reach out Your hand now and touch everything that belongs to him—he will surely curse You to Your face."
verses.1:12: And the LORD said to Satan, "Look, everything that belongs to him is in your hand; only against him do not reach out your hand." Then Satan went out from before the LORD.
verses.1:13: Now the day arrived when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine at the house of their firstborn brother.
verses.1:14: And a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the female donkeys were grazing alongside them,
verses.1:15: and the Sabeans fell upon them and took them away; and the young servants they struck down with the edge of the sword, and only I alone have escaped to report to you."
verses.1:16: While this one was still speaking, another arrived and said, "The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned among the sheep and the young servants and consumed them, and only I alone have escaped to report to you."
verses.1:17: While this one was still speaking, another arrived and said, "The Chaldeans formed three companies and raided the camels and took them away; and the young servants they struck down with the edge of the sword, and only I alone have escaped to report to you."
verses.1:18: While this one was still speaking, another arrived and said, "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine at the house of their firstborn brother,
verses.1:19: and look, a great wind came from across the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young people and they died; and only I alone have escaped to report to you."
verses.1:20: Then Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head; and he fell to the ground and bowed in worship.
verses.1:21: And he said, "Naked I came forth from my mother's womb, and naked I will return there. The LORD has given, and the LORD has taken; may the name of the LORD be blessed."
verses.1:22: Through all of this Job did not sin, nor did he ascribe wrongdoing to God.
verses.2:1: Now the day arrived when the sons of God came to take their stand before the LORD, and Satan came in their midst as well to take his stand before the LORD.
verses.2:2: And the LORD said to Satan, "From where are you coming?" Satan answered the LORD and said, "From ranging across the earth and from walking back and forth on it."
verses.2:3: Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you turned your thoughts to My servant Job? For there is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning aside from evil. He is still holding firmly to his integrity, even though you incited Me against him to swallow him up for nothing."
verses.2:4: Satan answered the LORD and said, "Skin for skin! Everything that belongs to a man he will give in exchange for his life.
verses.2:5: However, reach out Your hand now and touch his bone and his flesh—he will surely curse You to Your face."
verses.2:6: And the LORD said to Satan, "Look, he is in your hand; only preserve his life."
verses.2:7: Then Satan went out from before the LORD and struck Job with severe boils from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head.
verses.2:8: So he took himself a pottery shard to scrape himself with it, while he sat in the midst of the ashes.
verses.2:9: Then his wife said to him, "Are you still holding firmly to your integrity? Curse God and die!"
verses.2:10: But he said to her, "You are speaking just as one of the foolish women speaks. Should we accept what is good from God, and not accept what is bad?" Through all of this Job did not sin with his lips.
verses.2:11: Now Job's three friends heard about all this calamity that had come upon him, and they came, each from his own place—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite—and they arranged together to come to grieve with him and to comfort him.
verses.2:12: And they lifted their eyes from a distance and did not recognize him; so they lifted their voices and wept, each one tore his robe, and they tossed dust toward the heavens upon their heads.
verses.2:13: So they sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights, with no one speaking a word to him, because they saw that the pain was exceedingly great.
verses.3:1: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
verses.3:3: "Perish the day on which I was born, and the night that said, 'A male child has been conceived!'
verses.3:4: That day—let it be darkness! May God not seek it out from above, and may no daylight shine forth upon it.
verses.3:5: May darkness and the shadow of death lay claim to it; may a thick cloud settle over it; may the blacknesses of day terrify it.
verses.3:6: That night—let thick gloom seize it; let it not rejoice among the days of the year; into the number of the months let it not enter.
verses.3:7: Look, may that night be barren; may no shout of rejoicing come into it.
verses.3:8: May those who place curses on the day curse it, those who stand ready to awaken Leviathan.
verses.3:9: May the stars of its twilight grow dark; may it wait for light, yet there be none, and may it not look upon the eyelids of the dawn,
verses.3:10: because it did not close the doors of my mother's womb, nor conceal misery from my eyes.
verses.3:11: Why did I not die from the womb, and breathe my last when I came forth from the womb?
verses.3:12: Why did knees meet me, and why breasts, that I should nurse?
verses.3:13: For by now I would have lain down and stayed quiet; I would have fallen asleep, and then rest would be mine,
verses.3:14: with kings and earth's counselors, those who built ruins for themselves,
verses.3:15: or with rulers who possessed gold, those who filled their houses with silver.
verses.3:16: Or like a hidden miscarriage I would not exist, like infants who never saw light.
verses.3:17: There the wicked leave off turmoil, and there those worn out in strength rest.
verses.3:18: Together prisoners are at ease; they do not hear a taskmaster's voice.
verses.3:19: Both small and great are there, and a slave is free from his master.
verses.3:20: Why does He give light to one in misery, and life to those bitter of soul,
verses.3:21: who wait for death, yet it is not there, and dig after it more than for buried treasures,
verses.3:22: who rejoice even to exultation and are glad when they find a grave—
verses.3:23: to a man whose path is hidden, and whom God has hedged around?
verses.3:24: For before my bread my sighing comes, and my groans pour forth like water.
verses.3:25: For the dread I dreaded has come upon me, and what I feared comes to me.
verses.3:26: I have not been at ease, nor have I been quiet, nor have I rested—yet turmoil has come."
verses.4:1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite responded and said,
verses.4:2: "If one attempts a word with you, will you grow weary? Yet who is able to hold back words?
verses.4:3: Look, you instructed many, and you strengthened drooping hands.
verses.4:4: Your words raised up the one who was stumbling, and you fortified buckling knees.
verses.4:5: Yet now it comes to you, and you grow weary; it reaches even to you, and you are alarmed.
verses.4:6: Is not your fear your confidence, and your hope the blamelessness of your ways?
verses.4:7: Remember now, who has perished while innocent, and where have the upright been wiped out?
verses.4:8: Just as I have seen, those who plow iniquity and those who sow trouble reap it.
verses.4:9: At the breath of God they perish, and at the blast of His nostrils they come to an end.
verses.4:10: The roar of the lion and the sound of the fierce lion—and the teeth of young lions are broken out.
verses.4:11: The mighty lion perishes from lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness disperse.
verses.4:12: Now a word was conveyed to me in stealth, and my ear caught a whisper of it.
verses.4:13: In troubling thoughts from night visions, when deep sleep falls upon people,
verses.4:14: dread befell me, and trembling, and it filled all my bones with dread.
verses.4:15: Then a spirit swept across my face; the hair of my flesh bristled.
verses.4:16: It stopped, yet I could not recognize its appearance; a form was in front of my eyes; there was stillness, and I heard a voice:
verses.4:17: 'Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Or can a man be purer than his Maker?
verses.4:18: See, He does not place trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with folly;
verses.4:19: how much more the inhabitants of clay houses, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before a moth!
verses.4:20: From morning to evening they are shattered; with no one paying heed, they perish forever.
verses.4:21: Is not their tent cord pulled up within them? They die without wisdom.'"
verses.5:1: "Call now—is there anyone who answers you? And to whom among the holy ones will you turn?
verses.5:2: For resentment kills a fool, and envy puts a naive person to death.
verses.5:3: I myself saw a fool striking root, and at once I cursed his dwelling.
verses.5:4: His sons remain far from safety; they are crushed at the gate, and there is no rescuer.
verses.5:5: The hungry one eats his harvest and takes it even from among the thorns, and a snare pants after their wealth.
verses.5:6: For iniquity does not come out from the dust, and trouble does not sprout from the soil;
verses.5:7: rather, mankind is born for trouble, just as sparks soar high.
verses.5:8: Yet as for me, I would inquire of God, and I would lay my case before God,
verses.5:9: who does great things past searching out, wonders beyond number.
verses.5:10: He gives rain upon the face of the earth and sends waters upon the face of the open fields,
verses.5:11: to set the lowly in a high place, and mourners are raised high to safety.
verses.5:12: He thwarts the schemes of the crafty, and their hands accomplish no success.
verses.5:13: He traps the wise in their craftiness, and the counsel of the devious is rushed headlong.
verses.5:14: In daytime they encounter darkness, and as at night they grope at midday.
verses.5:15: So He saves the needy one from the sword out of their mouth and from the hand of the strong.
verses.5:16: So there is hope for the poor, and injustice closes its mouth.
verses.5:17: Look, blessed is the mortal whom God corrects; so do not reject the discipline of the Almighty.
verses.5:18: For He causes pain, yet He binds up; He wounds, yet His hands heal.
verses.5:19: In six distresses He will rescue you, and in seven no harm will touch you.
verses.5:20: In famine He will redeem you from death, and in battle from the hands of the sword.
verses.5:21: From the whip of the tongue you will be hidden, and you will not fear devastation when it comes.
verses.5:22: At devastation and hunger you will laugh, and do not fear the wild animals of the earth.
verses.5:23: For your covenant will be with the stones of the field, and the wild animals of the field will be at peace with you.
verses.5:24: And you will know that your tent is at peace, and you will examine your dwelling and find nothing missing.
verses.5:25: And you will know that your seed will be numerous, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
verses.5:26: You will come in mature vigor to the grave, like a grain stack brought up in its season.
verses.5:27: See, we have searched this out; it is so. Listen to it, and know it for yourself."
verses.6:2: "If only my vexation were truly weighed, and my calamity were lifted together in the scales!
verses.6:3: For then it would weigh more than the sand of the seas; for that reason my words have been reckless.
verses.6:4: For the Almighty's arrows are within me, whose venom my spirit is drinking; the terrors of God draw up against me.
verses.6:5: Does a wild donkey bray over fresh grass, or does an ox bellow over its fodder?
verses.6:6: Can something bland be eaten without salt, or is there any flavor in the juice of purslane?
verses.6:7: My soul has refused to touch them; they are like sickening food to me.
verses.6:8: If only my petition would come about, and God would grant my hope,
verses.6:9: that God would consent and crush me, that He would release His hand and cut me off!
verses.6:10: Then this would still be my comfort, and I would exult in anguish though He does not spare, for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.
verses.6:11: What strength do I have, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?
verses.6:12: Is the strength of stones my strength? Or is my flesh made of bronze?
verses.6:13: Have I truly no help within myself, and has resourcefulness been driven away from me?
verses.6:14: To the despairing one belongs loyal love from his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
verses.6:15: My brothers have acted treacherously like a wadi, like the channel of wadis that pass away,
verses.6:16: which are murky because of ice, upon which snow conceals itself.
verses.6:17: At the time they are scorched, they are cut off; when it grows hot, they are extinguished from their place.
verses.6:18: The paths of their course twist aside; they go up into the wasteland and perish.
verses.6:19: The caravans of Tema looked out; the traveling companies of Sheba waited in hope for them.
verses.6:20: They were put to shame because they had been confident; they came there and were humiliated.
verses.6:21: For now you have become nothing; you see terror and grow afraid.
verses.6:22: Have I indeed said, 'Give to me, and out of your resources pay a bribe on my behalf,
verses.6:23: and rescue me from the hand of a foe, and from the hand of ruthless men ransom me'?
verses.6:24: Instruct me, and I will keep silent; and make me understand where I have erred.
verses.6:25: How painful are words of uprightness! Yet what does reproving from you prove?
verses.6:26: Do you plan to reprove words, when the utterances of a despairing man are for the wind?
verses.6:27: Indeed, you would cast lots over an orphan, and haggle over your friend.
verses.6:28: And now, consent to look at me, for to your face I will surely not lie.
verses.6:29: Turn back now; let there be no injustice! And turn back again; my righteousness is in it.
verses.6:30: Is injustice on my tongue? Or does my palate not discern calamities?"
verses.7:1: "Is there not hard service for mortal man upon the earth, and are his days not like the days of a hired worker?
verses.7:2: Like a slave panting for the shade, and like a hired worker waiting for his wages,
verses.7:3: so I have been made to inherit months of futility, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.
verses.7:4: When I lie down, I say, 'When will I rise?' Yet the evening stretches out, and I have my fill of tossing until dawn.
verses.7:5: My flesh is clothed with maggots and clods of dust; my skin hardens and oozes.
verses.7:6: My days are faster than a weaver's shuttle, and they end without hope.
verses.7:7: Remember that my life is wind; my eye will not return to see good.
verses.7:8: The eye of the one who sees me will not look on me; Your eyes will be on me, and I will be no more.
verses.7:9: A cloud fades and goes away; so the one who descends to Sheol does not come up.
verses.7:10: He does not return to his house again, nor does his place recognize him anymore.
verses.7:11: I too will not hold back my mouth; I will speak out of the distress of my spirit; I will complain out of the bitterness of my soul.
verses.7:12: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that You place a watch over me?
verses.7:13: When I say, 'My couch will comfort me; my bed will lighten my complaint,'
verses.7:14: then You dismay me with dreams, and through visions You terrify me,
verses.7:15: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
verses.7:16: I despise it; I will not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are a vapor.
verses.7:17: What is mortal man, that You magnify him, and that You place Your heart upon him,
verses.7:18: and You inspect him morning by morning, and moment by moment You test him?
verses.7:19: For how long will You not look away from me, nor release me until I swallow my saliva?
verses.7:20: If I have sinned, what do I do to You, Watcher of mankind? Why have You made me a target for Yourself, so that I have become a burden to myself?
verses.7:21: And why do You not forgive my transgression and make my iniquity pass away? For soon I will lie down in the dust, and You will search diligently for me, but I will be no more."
verses.8:1: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.8:2: "How long will you utter these things, and will the words of your mouth be a powerful wind?
verses.8:3: Does God twist justice, or does the Almighty twist righteousness?
verses.8:4: If your children sinned against Him, then He gave them over into the hand of their transgression.
verses.8:5: If you yourself diligently seek God and plead with the Almighty for favor,
verses.8:6: if you are pure and upright, surely now He will awaken on your behalf and restore your righteous dwelling.
verses.8:7: And though your beginning was small, your end will flourish greatly.
verses.8:8: For ask now of the former generation, and set your mind on what their fathers searched out.
verses.8:9: For we are from yesterday and know nothing, because our days upon the earth are a shadow.
verses.8:10: Will they not teach you, speak to you, and bring forth words from their hearts?
verses.8:11: Can papyrus grow tall without a marsh? Can reeds flourish without water?
verses.8:12: While it is still in its fresh greenness and not plucked, it withers before all grass.
verses.8:13: Like this are the paths of all who forget God, and the hope of a godless man will perish,
verses.8:14: whose confidence snaps, and his trust is a spider's house.
verses.8:15: He leans on his house, yet it does not stand; he takes hold of it, yet it does not hold firm.
verses.8:16: He is lush before the sun, and his shoot spreads forth over his garden.
verses.8:17: Over a stone heap his roots are intertwined; he gazes upon a house of stones.
verses.8:18: If he is swallowed up from his place, then it will disown him: 'I have not seen you.'
verses.8:19: Look, this is the joy of his way, and from the dust others will sprout.
verses.8:20: Look, God will not reject one who is blameless, nor will He take hold of the hand of evildoers.
verses.8:21: He will still fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with joyful shouting.
verses.8:22: Those who hate you will put on shame, and the tent of the wicked will cease to be."
verses.9:2: "Indeed, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
verses.9:3: If one desires to contend with Him, he cannot answer Him one out of a thousand.
verses.9:4: He is wise of heart and mighty in strength; who has hardened himself against Him and remained unscathed?
verses.9:5: He is the one who moves mountains, and they do not know that He has overturned them in His anger;
verses.9:6: who shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars shudder;
verses.9:7: who speaks to the sun, and it does not shine forth, and seals off the stars;
verses.9:8: who stretches out the heavens by Himself and treads upon the heights of the sea;
verses.9:9: who makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the inner chambers of the south;
verses.9:10: who does great things past searching out, and wonders without number.
verses.9:11: Look, He passes by me, and I do not see; He glides on, and I do not discern Him.
verses.9:12: Look, He seizes; who can turn Him back? Who would say to Him, 'What are You doing?'
verses.9:13: God does not turn back His anger; the helpers of Rahab stooped low beneath Him.
verses.9:14: How much less can I answer Him, or select my words with Him?
verses.9:15: Even if I am righteous, I cannot answer; I must plead for favor with my judge.
verses.9:16: If I called out and He answered me, I would not believe that He was giving ear to my voice,
verses.9:17: for He crushes me with a storm and multiplies my wounds for no reason.
verses.9:18: He does not let me recover my breath, but He satiates me with bitterness.
verses.9:19: If it is a matter of strength, look, He is mighty; and if it is a matter of justice, who will summon me?
verses.9:20: Even if I am righteous, my own mouth would declare me guilty; I am blameless, yet it would declare me crooked.
verses.9:21: I am blameless; I have no regard for myself; I despise my life.
verses.9:22: It is all the same; therefore I say, 'The blameless and the wicked He destroys.'
verses.9:23: If a scourge brings death suddenly, He scoffs at the despair of the innocent.
verses.9:24: The earth has been given into the hand of the wicked; He veils the faces of its judges—if not He, then who is it?
verses.9:25: And my days are faster than a runner; they have fled, they have seen no good.
verses.9:26: They glide past like boats of reed, like an eagle swooping down upon prey.
verses.9:27: If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will lay aside my gloomy look and brighten up,'
verses.9:28: I dread all my pains; I know that You will not hold me guiltless.
verses.9:29: I will be found guilty; why then should I toil in vain?
verses.9:30: If I washed myself with snow water and cleansed my hands with lye,
verses.9:31: then You would immerse me in the pit, and my garments would detest me.
verses.9:32: For He is not a man like me, that I could answer Him, that we could come together into judgment.
verses.9:33: There is no arbiter between us who could place his hand upon the two of us.
verses.9:34: May He remove His rod from me, and may His dread not terrify me.
verses.9:35: Then I would speak, and I would not fear Him, for I am not so with myself."
verses.10:1: "My soul loathes my life; I will let loose my complaint within me; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.10:2: I will say to God, 'Do not pronounce me guilty; make known to me over what You contend with me.
verses.10:3: Is it good to You that You oppress, that You reject the toil of Your hands, while You shine forth upon the counsel of the wicked?
verses.10:4: Do You have eyes of flesh, or do You see as a mortal sees?
verses.10:5: Are Your days like the days of a mortal, or Your years like the days of a man,
verses.10:6: that You search for my iniquity and inquire after my sin,
verses.10:7: even though You know that I am not wicked, and there is no one who rescues from Your hand?
verses.10:8: Your hands shaped me and made me, yet You swallow me up altogether on every side.
verses.10:9: Remember, please, that You made me like clay; and will You bring me back to dust?
verses.10:10: Did You not pour me out as milk and congeal me like cheese?
verses.10:11: With skin and flesh You clothed me, and with bones and sinews You wove me together.
verses.10:12: Life and steadfast kindness You have shown to me, and Your watchful care has guarded my spirit.
verses.10:13: Yet these things You hid away in Your heart; I know that this was with You:
verses.10:14: If I sin, You keep watch over me, and You will not clear me of my iniquity.
verses.10:15: If I am wicked, woe to me; and even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head, filled with disgrace and gazing on my affliction.
verses.10:16: And if it rises up, like a lion You hunt me, and again You show Yourself wondrous against me.
verses.10:17: You renew Your witnesses against me and multiply Your indignation toward me; relays and an army are against me.
verses.10:18: And why did You bring me out from the womb? I should have breathed my last, and no eye would have seen me.
verses.10:19: I would have been as though I had never existed; from the womb to the grave I would have been carried.
verses.10:20: Are not my days few? Cease, then, and turn away from me, that I may brighten up a little,
verses.10:21: before I depart and do not return, to the land of darkness and the shadow of death,
verses.10:22: a land of gloom like pitch darkness, of the shadow of death with no order, where it shines like pitch darkness.'"
verses.11:1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said,
verses.11:2: "Should an abundance of words go unanswered, or a man of lips be vindicated?
verses.11:3: Should your empty boasts silence men, and should you scoff with no one to put you to shame?
verses.11:4: For you said, 'My teaching is pure, and I have been clean in Your eyes.'
verses.11:5: Yet if only God would speak and open His lips toward you,
verses.11:6: and declare to you the hidden things of wisdom—for sound wisdom is twofold! Know then that God overlooks for you some of your iniquity.
verses.11:7: Can you find the depths of God? Or can you attain to the boundary of the Almighty?
verses.11:8: The heights of heaven—what can you do? Deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
verses.11:9: Longer than the earth is its measure, and wider than the sea.
verses.11:10: If He sweeps past and imprisons, and convenes an assembly, then who can turn Him back?
verses.11:11: For He knows men of falsehood, and He sees wrongdoing—will He not take notice?
verses.11:12: But a hollow man will gain understanding when the colt of a wild donkey is born a human.
verses.11:13: If you direct your heart and spread out your palms to Him,
verses.11:14: if wrongdoing is in your hand, send it far away, and do not allow injustice to dwell in your tents;
verses.11:15: then indeed you will lift up your face without blemish, and you will be firmly established and will not fear.
verses.11:16: For you will forget trouble; you will recall it like waters that have passed by.
verses.11:17: And life will arise brighter than noonday; even if it grows dark, it will be like the morning.
verses.11:18: And you will be confident, for there is hope; you will search around and lie down in safety.
verses.11:19: And you will rest with no one to frighten you, and many will seek your favor.
verses.11:20: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, escape will perish from them, and their hope is the breathing out of life."
verses.12:2: "Surely you are the people, and with you wisdom will die!
verses.12:3: I too have a mind just as you do; I do not fall short of you. And who does not have things like these?
verses.12:4: I have become one who is a laughingstock to his friend, one who called upon God and He answered him—the righteous and blameless man is a laughingstock!
verses.12:5: For misfortune there is contempt in the thought of one at ease; it stands ready for those whose feet slip.
verses.12:6: The tents of plunderers are at peace, and security belongs to those who provoke God—to the one who brings a god in his hand.
verses.12:7: However, ask the beasts now, and they will instruct you; and the birds of the sky, and they will tell you;
verses.12:8: or speak to the earth, and it will instruct you, and the fish of the sea will report to you.
verses.12:9: Who does not know among all these that the hand of the LORD has done this,
verses.12:10: in whose hand is the life of every living creature and the breath of all human flesh?
verses.12:11: Does not the ear examine words, and the palate taste food for itself?
verses.12:12: With the aged is wisdom, and in length of days is understanding.
verses.12:13: With Him are wisdom and power; His are counsel and understanding.
verses.12:14: See, He tears down, and it will not be rebuilt; He shuts a man in, and it will not be opened.
verses.12:15: See, He holds back the waters, and they dry up; and He sends them out, and they overturn the earth.
verses.12:16: With Him are might and sound wisdom; His are the one who errs and the one who leads astray.
verses.12:17: He makes counselors walk stripped, and judges He makes into fools.
verses.12:18: He unties the bond of kings and binds a waistcloth around their waists.
verses.12:19: He makes priests walk stripped, and He overthrows the firmly established.
verses.12:20: He removes speech from the trustworthy, and the discernment of the elders He takes away.
verses.12:21: He pours out contempt upon nobles and loosens the sash of the mighty.
verses.12:22: He uncovers deep things from darkness and brings the shadow of death into light.
verses.12:23: He causes the nations to grow great, and He destroys them; He spreads out the nations, and He leads them away.
verses.12:24: He removes understanding from the leaders of the people of the earth and causes them to wander in a wasteland without a way.
verses.12:25: They grope in darkness without light, and He causes them to stagger like a drunkard."
verses.13:1: Look, all of it my eye has seen; my ear has heard and understood it.
verses.13:2: Just as you know, I also know; I do not fall short of you.
verses.13:3: However, I myself would speak to the Almighty, and I wish to argue with God.
verses.13:4: Yet you are plasterers of falsehood; all of you are worthless healers.
verses.13:5: If only you would remain utterly silent, and that would be wisdom for you!
verses.13:6: Listen, please, to my argument, and pay attention to the pleadings of my lips.
verses.13:7: Will you speak injustice for God, and for Him will you speak deceit?
verses.13:8: Will you show favoritism toward Him, or will you contend for God?
verses.13:9: Would it be good when He investigates you? Or as one deceives a mortal, will you deceive Him?
verses.13:10: He will certainly rebuke you if in secret you show favoritism.
verses.13:11: Will His majesty not terrify you, and His dread fall upon you?
verses.13:12: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes; your bulwarks are bulwarks of clay.
verses.13:13: Stay silent before me so that I myself may speak, and let come upon me whatever will.
verses.13:14: Why do I carry my flesh in my teeth and place my life in my hand?
verses.13:15: Even if He kills me, in Him I will hope; nevertheless, I will defend my ways to His face.
verses.13:16: This too will be my deliverance, for no godless person will come before Him.
verses.13:17: Listen intently to my speech, and let my declaration be in your ears.
verses.13:18: Look now, I have laid out a case; I know that I myself will be in the right.
verses.13:19: Who is the one who will contend with me? For then I would keep silent and expire.
verses.13:20: Only do not do two things to me; then I will not hide myself from Your face:
verses.13:21: Move Your hand far away from me, and do not let Your dread terrify me.
verses.13:22: Then call, and I myself will answer; or I will speak, and answer me back.
verses.13:23: How many iniquities and sins do I have? Make my transgression and my sin known to me.
verses.13:24: Why do You hide Your face and regard me as an enemy of Yours?
verses.13:25: Will You terrorize a blown leaf, and chase dry stubble?
verses.13:26: For You write down bitter things against me and cause me to inherit the iniquities of my youth.
verses.13:27: You place my feet in the stocks and keep watch over all my paths; You trace a boundary around the soles of my feet.
verses.13:28: And he wears out like a decaying thing, like a garment that a moth has eaten.
verses.14:1: Man, born of a woman, is short of days and filled with turmoil.
verses.14:2: Like a blossom he springs forth and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not endure.
verses.14:3: Do You open Your eye even on such a one, and bring me into judgment with Yourself?
verses.14:4: Who can produce what is clean from what is unclean? Not one.
verses.14:5: Since his days are fixed, the number of his months is with You, and You have set his bounds that he cannot cross,
verses.14:6: look away from him so that he may rest, until he completes his day like a hired worker.
verses.14:7: For a tree has hope: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its tender shoot will not cease.
verses.14:8: Even if its root grows old in the ground, and its stump dies in the dust,
verses.14:9: at the scent of water it will blossom and yield boughs like a sapling.
verses.14:10: Yet a man dies and lies powerless; a human expires, and where is he?
verses.14:11: Waters vanish from a sea, and a river grows parched and dries up;
verses.14:12: so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, they will not wake up or be roused from their sleep.
verses.14:13: If only You would conceal me in Sheol, hide me until Your anger turns away, appoint a limit for me, and remember me!
verses.14:14: If a man dies, will he live? All the days of my hard service I would wait until my relief comes.
verses.14:15: You would call, and I myself would answer You; You would yearn for the work of Your hands.
verses.14:16: For then You would count my steps; You would not watch over my sin.
verses.14:17: My transgression would be sealed in a pouch, and You would plaster over my iniquity.
verses.14:18: However, a falling mountain crumbles, and a rock shifts from its place;
verses.14:19: waters grind down stones; its torrents sweep away the dust of the earth; so You destroy the hope of a mortal.
verses.14:20: You overpower him forever, and he goes away; You alter his face and dismiss him.
verses.14:21: His sons gain honor, and he does not know; they sink low, and he does not notice them.
verses.14:22: Only his flesh aches upon him, and his soul mourns within him.
verses.15:1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied and said:
verses.15:2: "Should a wise man reply with knowledge of wind and fill his belly with the east wind,
verses.15:3: arguing with speech that is of no use, and with words by which he brings no benefit?
verses.15:4: In fact, you annul reverence and diminish meditation before God.
verses.15:5: For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the shrewd.
verses.15:6: Your mouth declares you guilty, and not I; and your lips bear witness against you.
verses.15:7: Were you the first man born, and before the hills were you brought forth?
verses.15:8: Do you listen in the inner council of God, and restrict wisdom to yourself?
verses.15:9: What do you know that we do not know, or understand that is not with us?
verses.15:10: Both the gray-haired and the elderly are among us, greater in days than your father.
verses.15:11: Are the comforts of God too slight for you, and a gentle word with you?
verses.15:12: Why does your heart sweep you away, and why are your eyes flashing,
verses.15:13: that you turn your spirit against God and send forth words from your mouth?
verses.15:14: What is mortal man, that he could be pure, or that one born of a woman could be righteous?
verses.15:15: See, He places no trust in His holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in His eyes;
verses.15:16: how much less one who is abhorrent and tainted, a man who drinks unrighteousness like water!
verses.15:17: I will tell you; listen to me, and what I have observed I will recount,
verses.15:18: what wise men declare, and have not concealed, from their fathers.
verses.15:19: To them alone the land was given, and no foreigner passed through their midst:
verses.15:20: All the days of a wicked man he writhes in torment, and numbered years are reserved for the ruthless.
verses.15:21: The sound of terrors is in his ears; amid peace a plunderer comes upon him.
verses.15:22: He has no trust that he will return from darkness, and he is spied out for the sword.
verses.15:23: He roams about for bread, 'Where is it?' He knows that a day of darkness is prepared at his hand.
verses.15:24: Distress and anguish strike him with terror; they overpower him like a king prepared for the onslaught,
verses.15:25: because he extended his hand against God and acts defiantly against the Almighty;
verses.15:26: he charges against Him with outstretched neck, with the thick bosses of his shields,
verses.15:27: since he covered his face with his fat and formed thick fat on his flanks.
verses.15:28: And he has settled in ruined cities, houses that no one inhabits, which are set for heaps of rubble.
verses.15:29: He will not grow rich, and his wealth will not stand, nor will their possessions extend over the earth.
verses.15:30: He will not depart from darkness; a flame will dry up his young shoot, and he will pass away by the breath of His mouth.
verses.15:31: Let him not, deluded, trust in futility, for futility will be his recompense.
verses.15:32: Before his day it will be fulfilled, and his palm frond will not be green.
verses.15:33: Like the vine he will strip off his unripe grapes, and like the olive tree he will shed his blossoms.
verses.15:34: For the assembly of the godless is sterile, and fire devours the tents of bribery.
verses.15:35: They conceive trouble and bear iniquity, and their belly prepares deceit."
verses.16:2: "I have heard many things like these; all of you are troublesome comforters.
verses.16:3: Is there an end to words of wind, or what goads you that you reply?
verses.16:4: I also could speak as you do, if your soul were in place of my soul; I could string words together against you and shake my head over you.
verses.16:5: I would encourage you with my mouth, and the sympathy of my lips would bring relief.
verses.16:6: If I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I refrain, what departs from me?
verses.16:7: Surely now He has worn me down; You have devastated all my company.
verses.16:8: And You have shriveled me, and it has become a witness; my gauntness has risen up against me; to my face it testifies.
verses.16:9: His wrath has torn and hated me; He has gnashed against me with His teeth; my foe sharpens His eyes at me.
verses.16:10: They have opened wide their mouths against me; in reproach they have struck my cheeks; together they throng against me.
verses.16:11: God delivers me over to the unjust, and into the hands of the wicked He hurls me.
verses.16:12: I was undisturbed, and He shattered me; He gripped me by my neck and smashed me to pieces, and He stood me up for Himself as a target.
verses.16:13: His archers encircle me; He cleaves my kidneys and shows no pity; He pours my gall out onto the ground.
verses.16:14: He breaches me with breach upon breach; He charges at me like a mighty warrior.
verses.16:15: I have stitched sackcloth onto my skin and plunged my horn into the dust.
verses.16:16: My face is inflamed from weeping, and deep gloom is on my eyelids,
verses.16:17: even though no violence is in my palms, and my prayer is pure.
verses.16:18: Earth, do not cover my blood, and let there be no halting place for my outcry.
verses.16:19: Even now, look, in the heavens is my witness, and the one who bears witness for me is in the heights.
verses.16:20: My friends are my mockers; to God my eye sheds tears,
verses.16:21: that one might plead for a man with God, as a son of man for his friend.
verses.16:22: For a few years will come, and I will walk a path from which I will not return."
verses.17:1: "My spirit is ruined, my days are snuffed out; tombs await me.
verses.17:2: Surely mockers are beside me, and my eye lodges on their provocation.
verses.17:3: Set down a pledge, please; stand surety for me with Yourself! Who is there who will strike hands with mine?
verses.17:4: For You have hidden their heart from insight; therefore You will not exalt them.
verses.17:5: One who denounces friends for a share—the eyes of his children will fail.
verses.17:6: He has set me as a byword to the peoples, and I have become one in whose face people spit.
verses.17:7: My eye has dimmed from grief, and all my limbs are like a shadow.
verses.17:8: The upright are horrified at this, and the innocent rouses himself against the godless.
verses.17:9: Yet the righteous holds fast to his way, and the one with clean hands increases in strength.
verses.17:10: However, turn back and come again, all of you, please; I will not find a wise man among you.
verses.17:11: My days have gone by; my plans are torn apart, the desires of my heart.
verses.17:12: They make night into day; light is near in the face of darkness.
verses.17:13: If I hope for Sheol to be my house, and spread out my couch in the darkness,
verses.17:14: if I call out to the pit, 'You are my father,' and to the maggot, 'My mother and my sister,'
verses.17:15: where then is my hope? As for my hope, who will see it?
verses.17:16: Will it go down to the bars of Sheol, when there is rest together in the dust?"
verses.18:1: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied and said:
verses.18:2: "How long until you put an end to words? Show discernment, and afterward we will speak.
verses.18:3: Why are we reckoned as beasts? Why are we dull in your eyes?
verses.18:4: You who tear yourself in your rage—shall the earth be abandoned for your sake, or a rock be shifted from its place?
verses.18:5: Surely the light of the wicked dies out, and the flame of his fire will not glow.
verses.18:6: The light grows dark in his tent, and his lamp above him dies out.
verses.18:7: The strides of his vigor are cramped, and his own counsel casts him down.
verses.18:8: For he is driven into a net by his own feet, and he walks about over netting.
verses.18:9: A trap catches him by the heel; a snare holds fast upon him.
verses.18:10: Concealed in the ground is a noose for him, and a trap for him upon the path.
verses.18:11: On all sides terrors horrify him, and drive him at his heels.
verses.18:12: His vigor grows famished, and disaster stands ready for his fall.
verses.18:13: It devours the parts of his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.
verses.18:14: He is torn away from his tent, his security, and marched to the king of terrors.
verses.18:15: What does not belong to him dwells in his tent; sulfur is strewn over his dwelling.
verses.18:16: Below, his roots dry out, and above, his bough withers.
verses.18:17: His remembrance perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the open country.
verses.18:18: They thrust him out of light into darkness, and banish him from the world.
verses.18:19: He has neither offspring nor grandchild among his people, and no survivor in his dwelling places.
verses.18:20: People of the west are stunned at his day, and those of the east are gripped with horror.
verses.18:21: Indeed, these are the dwellings of the wrongdoer, and this is the place of the one who does not know God."
verses.19:2: "How long will you grieve my soul and crush me with words?
verses.19:3: These ten times you have humiliated me; you are not ashamed to mistreat me.
verses.19:4: And even if indeed I have erred, with me my error lodges.
verses.19:5: If truly you exalt yourselves over me and argue my disgrace against me,
verses.19:6: then know that God has wronged me and drawn His hunting net around me.
verses.19:7: Look, I shout, 'Violence!' yet I go unanswered; I cry out for help, yet there is no justice.
verses.19:8: He has walled off my way so that I cannot pass through, and He places darkness over my paths.
verses.19:9: He has stripped my glory off me and taken away the crown of my head.
verses.19:10: He demolishes me all around, and I am gone; like a tree He uproots my hope.
verses.19:11: He has kindled His wrath against me and regards me as one of His adversaries.
verses.19:12: Together His troops advance; they build up their road against me and encamp all around my tent.
verses.19:13: He has placed my brothers far away from me, and those who know me are utterly alienated from me.
verses.19:14: My relatives have held back, and my close companions have forgotten me.
verses.19:15: Those staying in my house and my female servants regard me as a stranger; in their eyes I have become a foreigner.
verses.19:16: I call out to my servant, yet he does not reply; with my own mouth I implore him.
verses.19:17: My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to the sons of my womb.
verses.19:18: Even young boys scorn me; when I stand up, they speak against me.
verses.19:19: All the men of my inner circle detest me, and the ones I loved have turned against me.
verses.19:20: To my skin and to my flesh my bone clings, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
verses.19:21: Show me pity, show me pity, you friends of mine, for the hand of God has struck me!
verses.19:22: Why do you pursue me like God, and are not sated with my flesh?
verses.19:23: If only my words were written down now! If only they were inscribed in a scroll,
verses.19:24: with an iron stylus and lead, carved into the rock forever!
verses.19:25: Yet I myself know that my Redeemer is alive, and at the last He will rise upon the dust.
verses.19:26: And after this skin of mine has been stripped away, still from my flesh I will gaze upon God,
verses.19:27: whom I myself will gaze upon for myself, and my eyes will see, and not a stranger. My inmost being fails within my chest!
verses.19:28: If you say, 'How shall we pursue him?' and that the root of the matter is found in me,
verses.19:29: fear the sword for yourselves, for fury brings the penalties of the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment."
verses.20:1: Then Zophar the Naamathite responded and said,
verses.20:2: "Therefore my restless thoughts bring me a reply, even on account of the urgency within me.
verses.20:3: I hear a correction that disgraces me, and a spirit from my understanding answers me.
verses.20:4: Do you know this from ancient times, since mankind was placed upon the earth,
verses.20:5: that the joyous shouting of the wicked is brief, and the gladness of the godless is only for an instant?
verses.20:6: Even if his stature ascends to the heavens, and his head reaches to the clouds,
verses.20:7: like his own dung he will perish forever; those who saw him will say, 'Where is he?'
verses.20:8: Like a dream he will fly away, and they will not find him; he will be driven away like a vision of the night.
verses.20:9: The eye that caught sight of him will not do so again, nor will his place look upon him any longer.
verses.20:10: His sons will seek to appease the poor, and his own hands will restore his wealth.
verses.20:11: His bones are full of his youth, yet it will lie down with him upon the dust.
verses.20:12: Though evil tastes sweet in his mouth, and he conceals it beneath his tongue,
verses.20:13: though he spares it and will not abandon it, holding it back within his palate,
verses.20:14: yet his food in his stomach turns into the venom of cobras inside him.
verses.20:15: He has swallowed wealth, yet he will vomit it up; God will drive it out from his belly.
verses.20:16: The poison of cobras he will suck; a viper's tongue will kill him.
verses.20:17: He will not gaze at the streams, the rivers, the torrents of honey and curds.
verses.20:18: He returns what he toiled for and will not swallow it; for all the wealth of his trading, he will not exult.
verses.20:19: Because he crushed and abandoned the poor, he plundered a house that he did not build.
verses.20:20: Because he knew no quietness in his belly, he will save nothing of what he treasures.
verses.20:21: Nothing is left from his devouring; therefore his prosperity will not last.
verses.20:22: When his plenty is full, he will be hard-pressed; the hand of every afflicted person will come upon him.
verses.20:23: When he is about to fill his belly, He will unleash against him His burning anger, and will rain it down upon him as his food.
verses.20:24: He will flee from an iron weapon, yet a bow of bronze will pierce him through.
verses.20:25: He pulls it out, and it emerges from his back, and the gleaming point comes from his gallbladder; terrors are upon him.
verses.20:26: Total darkness lies hidden for his treasured stores; an unfanned fire will consume him, and what remains in his tent will come to ruin.
verses.20:27: The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth rises against him.
verses.20:28: The yield of his house will be carried away, flowing off on the day of His anger.
verses.20:29: This is a wicked man's allotment from God, and the inheritance appointed for him from God."
verses.21:2: "Listen intently to my speech, and let this be your consolation.
verses.21:3: Bear with me while I myself speak, and once I have spoken, you may mock.
verses.21:4: As for me, is my complaint aimed at man? Or why should my spirit not grow impatient?
verses.21:5: Turn to me and be astounded, and place your hand over your mouth.
verses.21:6: Even when I remember, I am terrified, and trembling grips my flesh.
verses.21:7: Why do the wicked go on living, grow old, and even become mighty in power?
verses.21:8: Their offspring stand established in their presence along with them, and their descendants are before their eyes.
verses.21:9: Their houses are at peace, free from dread, and God's rod is not upon them.
verses.21:10: His bull breeds and does not fail; his cow calves safely and does not miscarry.
verses.21:11: They send their little ones out like a flock, and their children leap about.
verses.21:12: They lift up their voices with tambourine and lyre, and they rejoice at the sound of the flute.
verses.21:13: They finish their days in prosperity, and in an instant they descend to Sheol.
verses.21:14: Yet they say to God, 'Turn away from us! We have no desire for the knowledge of Your ways.
verses.21:15: What is the Almighty, that we should serve Him? And what benefit do we gain if we appeal to Him?'
verses.21:16: See, their prosperity is not in their own hand; the counsel of the wicked stays far from me.
verses.21:17: How often does the lamp of the wicked go out, and does their disaster come upon them, and does He apportion pains in His anger?
verses.21:18: Are they like straw before the wind, and like chaff that a whirlwind steals away?
verses.21:19: God stores up his iniquity for his sons? Let Him repay him directly, so that he may know it!
verses.21:20: Let his own eyes see his ruin, and let him drink from the fury of the Almighty.
verses.21:21: For what interest does he have in his house after him, when the number of his months has been cut off?
verses.21:22: Will anyone teach knowledge to God, when He Himself judges those on high?
verses.21:23: One dies in the fullness of his vigor, completely tranquil and at ease;
verses.21:24: his pails are filled with milk, and the marrow of his bones is moistened.
verses.21:25: And another dies with a bitter soul, never having eaten of prosperity.
verses.21:26: Together they lie down upon the dust, and maggots cover over them.
verses.21:27: Look, I know your thoughts, and the plots with which you do me wrong.
verses.21:28: For you say, 'Where is the nobleman's house, and where is the tent of the dwellings of the wicked?'
verses.21:29: Have you not questioned those who pass along the road, and do you not recognize their evidence,
verses.21:30: that the evil man is spared on the day of disaster, and they are led away on the day of wrath?
verses.21:31: Who will tell him his way to his face? And for what he has done, who will repay him?
verses.21:32: And he is carried to the graves, and over the burial mound watch is kept.
verses.21:33: Sweet to him are the clods of the valley; after him all mankind follows along, and before him they are without number.
verses.21:34: How then can you console me with emptiness, when in your replies there remains only deceit?"
verses.22:1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied and said,
verses.22:2: "Can a strong man be of benefit to God? Rather, a discerning man benefits himself.
verses.22:3: Is it a delight to the Almighty when you are righteous, or a gain when you make your ways blameless?
verses.22:4: Is it on account of your reverence that He rebukes you and comes with you into judgment?
verses.22:5: Is your wickedness not great, and is there no end to your iniquities?
verses.22:6: For you took pledges from your brothers for nothing, and stripped off the garments of the naked.
verses.22:7: You gave no water for the weary to drink, and from the hungry you kept back bread.
verses.22:8: As for the man of power, the land was his, and the honored man lived in it.
verses.22:9: Widows you sent away empty-handed, and the arms of the fatherless were crushed.
verses.22:10: Therefore snares are on every side of you, and sudden dread terrifies you,
verses.22:11: or darkness, so you cannot see, and a flood of waters covers you.
verses.22:12: Is God not in the height of the heavens? And look at the topmost stars, how high they are!
verses.22:13: Yet you say, 'What does God know? Does He judge through dense darkness?
verses.22:14: Thick clouds are a covering for Him, so He does not see, and He walks about on the circle of the heavens.'
verses.22:15: Will you keep the path of old that men of iniquity have trodden,
verses.22:16: who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was washed away by a river,
verses.22:17: who said to God, 'Turn away from us!' and, 'What can the Almighty do to them?'
verses.22:18: Yet He Himself filled their houses with good things; still, the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
verses.22:19: The righteous see and rejoice, and the innocent person scorns them:
verses.22:20: 'Indeed, our adversaries have been wiped out, and fire has consumed their abundance.'
verses.22:21: Now become reconciled with Him and be at peace; through these things good will come to you.
verses.22:22: Accept instruction now from His mouth, and place His words in your heart.
verses.22:23: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up; put injustice far from your tent,
verses.22:24: and set gold ore in the dust, and the gold of Ophir as stones of the streambeds,
verses.22:25: then the Almighty will be your gold ore, and the finest silver for you.
verses.22:26: For then you will take delight in the Almighty, and lift your face to God.
verses.22:27: You will pray to Him and He will listen to you, and you will fulfill your vows.
verses.22:28: You will decree a matter, and it will stand for you, and upon your ways light will shine.
verses.22:29: When people are brought low, you will say, 'There is lifting up!' and He will save the one with downcast eyes.
verses.22:30: He will rescue the one who is not innocent, and he will be rescued by the purity of your hands."
verses.23:2: "Even today my complaint is rebellious; my hand is heavy despite my groaning.
verses.23:3: If only I knew where I could find Him, that I might come all the way to His seat!
verses.23:4: I would set a case in order before Him, and I would fill my mouth with arguments.
verses.23:5: I would know the words He would answer me, and discern what He would say to me.
verses.23:6: Would He contend with me in greatness of strength? No! Surely He would give attention to me.
verses.23:7: There an upright person could reason with Him, and I would be set free forever from my Judge.
verses.23:8: See, I go forward, yet He is not there, and backward, yet I do not discern Him;
verses.23:9: on the left, when He is working, I cannot glimpse Him; He turns to the right, yet I do not see Him.
verses.23:10: Yet He knows the way that is with me; when He has tested me, I will emerge like gold.
verses.23:11: My foot has held firmly to His step; His way I have kept and have not turned aside.
verses.23:12: From the command of His lips I have not departed; more than my allotted portion, I have stored up the words of His mouth.
verses.23:13: Yet He is One, and who can turn Him back? What His soul desires, He does.
verses.23:15: Therefore I am terrified before His face; when I reflect, I dread Him.
verses.23:16: And God has caused my heart to grow faint, and the Almighty has terrified me,
verses.23:17: for I was not cut off before the darkness, nor did He conceal the thick gloom from my face."
verses.24:1: "Why are times not kept in reserve by the Almighty, and why do those who know Him not witness His days?
verses.24:2: People shift boundary markers; they seize a flock and pasture it.
verses.24:3: The donkey of the fatherless they drive away; they take a widow's ox in pledge.
verses.24:4: They push the needy off the road; all together, the poor of the land are forced to hide.
verses.24:5: Look, like wild donkeys in the wilderness, they go out to their labor, searching diligently for food; the barren plain is bread to him for the children.
verses.24:6: In the field they reap his fodder, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
verses.24:7: Naked they pass the night without clothing, and there is no covering in the cold.
verses.24:8: By the downpour of the mountains they are drenched, and without shelter they hug a rock.
verses.24:9: They snatch away the fatherless from the breast, and they take a pledge against the poor.
verses.24:10: Naked they walk about without clothing, and hungry they carry sheaves.
verses.24:11: Between their walls they press out oil; they tread winepresses, yet they are thirsty.
verses.24:12: Out of the city men groan, and the soul of the wounded cries for help; yet God charges no wrong.
verses.24:13: They are among those who rebel against the light; they do not recognize its ways, and they do not remain in its paths.
verses.24:14: At daybreak the murderer rises; he kills the poor and the needy, and during the night he is like a thief.
verses.24:15: And the eye of the adulterer watches for dusk, saying, 'No eye will see me,' and he puts a covering over his face.
verses.24:16: In the darkness one digs through houses; by day they seal themselves in; they do not know the light.
verses.24:17: For to all of them alike, deep darkness is morning, because each recognizes the terrors of deep darkness.
verses.24:18: He is swift on the surface of the waters; their portion in the land is cursed; he does not turn toward the way of the vineyards.
verses.24:19: Drought and heat alike carry off the snow waters, just as Sheol does those who have sinned.
verses.24:20: The womb forgets him, the worm feeds sweetly on him; he is remembered no more, and injustice is broken like a tree.
verses.24:21: He preys on the barren woman who bears no child, and to the widow he does no good.
verses.24:22: Yet He prolongs the mighty by His power; he rises up when he has no assurance of life.
verses.24:23: He grants him security, and he is supported; and His eyes are upon their ways.
verses.24:24: They rise high for a little while, and then he is no more; they are laid low, gathered in like all others, and like the head of an ear of grain they are cut off.
verses.24:25: And if it is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my speech to nothing?"
verses.25:1: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.25:2: "Dominion and dread are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.
verses.25:3: Is there a count for His troops? And over whom does His light not arise?
verses.25:4: And how can a mortal be righteous with God, and how can someone born of a woman be pure?
verses.25:5: Look, even the moon does not shine, nor are the stars pure in His eyes;
verses.25:6: how much less a mortal, a maggot, and a son of man, a worm!"
verses.26:2: "How you have helped one without strength! You have rescued the arm without might!
verses.26:3: How you have advised one without wisdom, and made sound insight known in abundance!
verses.26:4: To whom have you declared words, and whose breath went out from you?
verses.26:5: The shades writhe beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.
verses.26:6: Sheol is bare before Him, and there is no covering for Abaddon.
verses.26:7: He stretches the north over emptiness; He suspends the earth upon nothing.
verses.26:8: He bundles up the waters in His thick clouds, and the cloud is not split beneath them.
verses.26:9: He shrouds the face of the throne; He spreads His cloud across it.
verses.26:10: He has traced a circular boundary over the face of the waters, to the limit of light with darkness.
verses.26:11: The pillars of the heavens are shaken, and they are stunned at His rebuke.
verses.26:12: By His strength He stirred up the sea, and by His understanding He crushed Rahab.
verses.26:13: By His breath the heavens became bright; His hand pierced through the fleeing serpent.
verses.26:14: Look, these are the edges of His ways, and what a whisper of a word we hear of Him! And the thunder of His mighty deeds, who can comprehend?"
verses.27:1: And Job continued to take up his discourse and said:
verses.27:2: "As God lives, who has removed my right, and the Almighty, who has brought bitterness to my soul—
verses.27:3: for as long as my breath is within me, and God's spirit is in my nostrils—
verses.27:4: my lips will never speak wrongdoing, and my tongue will never murmur deceit.
verses.27:5: Far be it from me to pronounce you in the right! Until I breathe my last, I will not remove my integrity from myself.
verses.27:6: I hold firmly to my righteousness and will not release it; my heart does not blame me for any of my days.
verses.27:7: Let my enemy be like a wicked man, and the one who rises against me like a wrongdoer.
verses.27:8: For what hope does a godless man have, though he makes unjust gain, when God draws out his soul?
verses.27:9: Will God heed his outcry when distress comes over him?
verses.27:10: Or will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call out to God at all times?
verses.27:11: I will instruct you about the hand of God; I will not hide what is with the Almighty.
verses.27:12: Look, all of you yourselves have seen it; and why then do you act so futilely?
verses.27:13: This is the share of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance that ruthless men receive from the Almighty:
verses.27:14: Though his sons multiply, they are for the sword, and his offspring will not have their fill of bread.
verses.27:15: His survivors will be buried by death, and his widows will not weep.
verses.27:16: If he heaps up silver like the dust and prepares clothing like the clay,
verses.27:17: he may prepare it, yet a righteous man will wear it, and an innocent man will divide up the silver.
verses.27:18: He has built his house like the moth, and like a shelter a watchman has made.
verses.27:19: He lies down rich, yet he will not be gathered; he opens his eyes, and he is no more.
verses.27:20: Like the waters, terrors overtake him; by night a whirlwind steals him away.
verses.27:21: The east wind bears him off and he departs, and it sweeps him from his place.
verses.27:22: And it hurls at him and does not spare; from its hand he flees headlong.
verses.27:23: It claps its palms over him and whistles at him out of his place."
verses.28:1: Indeed, there is a source for silver, and a place for gold where they refine it.
verses.28:2: Iron is taken out of dust, and stone is smelted into copper.
verses.28:3: He sets an end to darkness, and to every extremity he searches out the stone of gloom and deep shadow.
verses.28:4: He breaks open a shaft away from any dweller; forgotten by any foot, they dangle far from mortals, they sway.
verses.28:5: The earth—bread comes forth from it, yet underneath it is overturned as by fire.
verses.28:6: Its stones are a place of sapphire, and dust of gold belongs to it.
verses.28:7: A path—no bird of prey knows it, nor has the eye of the falcon glimpsed it;
verses.28:8: majestic beasts have not trodden upon it, nor has any lion passed across it.
verses.28:9: He stretches out his hand against the flint; he overturns mountains from the root.
verses.28:10: He splits open channels in the rocks, and his eye sees all that is precious.
verses.28:11: He binds up streams from trickling, and he brings what is hidden forth to light.
verses.28:12: Yet wisdom—from where can it be found? And where then is the place of understanding?
verses.28:13: No mortal knows its worth, and it is not to be found in the land of the living.
verses.28:14: The abyss says, "It is not within me," and the sea says, "It is not with me."
verses.28:15: Solid gold will not be given in return for it, nor will silver be weighed out for its price.
verses.28:16: It cannot be appraised against the gold of Ophir, against precious onyx or sapphire.
verses.28:17: Gold and glass cannot match it, nor can a vessel of refined gold be its exchange.
verses.28:18: Coral and crystal will not be mentioned, and the possession of wisdom is above pearls.
verses.28:19: The topaz of Cush cannot match it; against pure gold it cannot be appraised.
verses.28:20: Yet wisdom—from where does it come? And where then is the place of understanding?
verses.28:21: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, and from the birds of the heavens it is concealed.
verses.28:22: Abaddon and Death say, "With our ears we heard its rumor."
verses.28:23: God understands its way, and He Himself knows its place.
verses.28:24: For He gazes to the ends of the earth and sees beneath all the heavens.
verses.28:25: When He made a weight for the wind and gauged the waters by measure,
verses.28:26: when He made a statute for the rain and a way for the flash of thunder,
verses.28:27: then He saw it and recounted it; He established it and searched it out as well.
verses.28:28: And He said to mankind, "See, the fear of the Lord—that is wisdom, and turning aside from evil is understanding."
verses.29:1: Then Job lifted up his discourse once more and said,
verses.29:2: "If only I were as in former months, as in the days when God guarded me,
verses.29:3: when He made His lamp shine above my head, and I walked through darkness by His light,
verses.29:4: just as I was in the days of my prime, when the intimate fellowship of God was over my tent,
verses.29:5: while the Almighty was still with me, with my children all around me,
verses.29:6: when my footsteps were bathed in cream, and the rock poured out streams of oil beside me!
verses.29:7: When I went out to the gate by the city, when I set up my seat in the open square,
verses.29:8: young men saw me and drew back, and the elderly rose up and stood.
verses.29:9: Princes held back their words and placed a hand over their mouth.
verses.29:10: The voice of nobles was stilled, and their tongue clung to their palate.
verses.29:11: For the ear heard and pronounced me blessed, and the eye saw and bore witness for me,
verses.29:12: because I rescued the poor who cried out, and the fatherless who had no helper.
verses.29:13: The blessing of one who was perishing came upon me, and I made the heart of the widow sing with joy.
verses.29:14: I wore righteousness, and it clothed me; like a robe and turban was my justice.
verses.29:15: Eyes I was for the blind, and feet I was for the lame.
verses.29:16: A father I was for the needy, and I searched out the dispute of one I did not know.
verses.29:17: And I shattered the fangs of the wrongdoer, and from his teeth I flung the prey.
verses.29:18: And I said, 'I will breathe my last in my nest, and like the sand I will multiply days;
verses.29:19: my root is open to the waters, and dew will spend the night on my branch;
verses.29:20: my glory is fresh with me, and my bow in my hand will renew itself.'
verses.29:21: They listened to me and waited expectantly, and they were silent for my counsel.
verses.29:22: After my word they would not speak again, and upon them my speech fell in drops.
verses.29:23: They waited expectantly for me as for the rain, and opened their mouth wide for spring rain.
verses.29:24: When I smiled at them, they could not believe it, and they did not cause the light of my face to fall.
verses.29:25: I chose their way and sat at the head, and I dwelt like a king amid the troops, like one who consoles mourners."
verses.30:1: But now those younger than I in days laugh at me, whose fathers I scorned to place with the dogs of my flock.
verses.30:2: Indeed, what use to me was the strength of their hands? Vigor had perished from them.
verses.30:3: Gaunt from want and famine, they gnaw the parched earth by night in ruin and wasteland.
verses.30:4: They pluck saltwort among the bushes, and the root of broom shrubs is their food.
verses.30:5: They are driven out from the community; people shout at them as at a thief.
verses.30:6: In the clefts of the ravines they must dwell, in holes of the earth and the rocks.
verses.30:7: Among the bushes they bray; under the nettles they are huddled together.
verses.30:8: Sons of a fool, yes, sons without a name, they have been scourged out of the land.
verses.30:9: And now I have become their song, and to them I am a byword.
verses.30:10: They detest me, they keep far from me, and they do not hold back from spitting in my face.
verses.30:11: For He has loosed my cord and afflicted me, and they have cast off the bridle before me.
verses.30:12: On the right the rabble rises; they push my feet aside, and they cast up against me their paths of destruction.
verses.30:13: They tear up my path; they advance my downfall, with no one to help them.
verses.30:14: As through a wide breach they come; amid the ruin they roll onward.
verses.30:15: Terrors are turned upon me; they chase my dignity like the wind, and like a cloud my welfare has passed away.
verses.30:16: And now my soul pours itself out within me; days of affliction grip me.
verses.30:17: Night pierces my bones from me, and my gnawing pains do not rest.
verses.30:18: By great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me about like the collar of my tunic.
verses.30:19: He has thrown me into the mud, and I have come to resemble dust and ashes.
verses.30:20: I cry out to You for help, and You do not answer me; I stand up, and You gaze at me.
verses.30:21: You turn cruel toward me; with the might of Your hand You assail me.
verses.30:22: You lift me up to the wind and make me ride on it, and You melt away my substance.
verses.30:23: For I know that You will bring me back to death, and to the house of assembly for all the living.
verses.30:24: Yet surely one does not stretch out a hand against a heap of ruins, when in his calamity there is a cry for help.
verses.30:25: Did I not weep for the one whose day was hard? Did not my soul grieve for the needy?
verses.30:26: Yet I hoped for good, and evil came; I waited for light, and thick darkness came.
verses.30:27: My inward parts boil and are not still; days of affliction confront me.
verses.30:28: I walk about blackened, with no sun; I rise in the assembly and cry out for help.
verses.30:29: I have become a brother to jackals, and a friend to ostriches.
verses.30:30: My skin has blackened upon me, and my bones burn with heat.
verses.30:31: And my lyre has turned to mourning, and my flute to the voice of those who weep.
verses.31:1: I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look intently upon a virgin?
verses.31:2: And what is the portion from God above, and the inheritance from the Almighty on high?
verses.31:3: Is not calamity for the unjust, and disaster for those who do iniquity?
verses.31:4: Does not He Himself see my ways, and count all my steps?
verses.31:5: If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried toward deceit,
verses.31:6: let Him weigh me in scales of righteousness, and let God know my integrity.
verses.31:7: If my step has turned aside from the way, and my heart has walked after my eyes, and any stain has clung to my palms,
verses.31:8: then let me sow and another eat, and let my produce be uprooted.
verses.31:9: If my heart has been enticed toward a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbor's door,
verses.31:10: then let my wife grind for another, and let others kneel over her.
verses.31:11: For that would be depravity, and it would be an iniquity for judges.
verses.31:12: For it is a fire that would consume as far as Abaddon, and uproot all my harvest.
verses.31:13: If I have rejected the cause of my male servant or my female servant when they contended with me,
verses.31:14: what then would I do when God rises up? And when He calls to account, what would I answer Him?
verses.31:15: Did not the One who made me in the womb make him, and did not One fashion us in the womb?
verses.31:16: If I have withheld from the poor their desire, or caused the eyes of a widow to fail,
verses.31:17: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless did not eat from it—
verses.31:18: for from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother's womb I have guided her—
verses.31:19: if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or a needy person with no covering,
verses.31:20: if his loins have not blessed me, and if he did not warm himself with the fleece of my sheep,
verses.31:21: if I have lifted my hand against the fatherless because I saw my help in the gate,
verses.31:22: then let my shoulder fall away from its socket, and let my arm be broken from its bone.
verses.31:23: For calamity from God was a dread to me, and because of His majesty I could not stand.
verses.31:24: If I have made gold my confidence, or said to fine gold, "You are my trust,"
verses.31:25: if I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gained much,
verses.31:26: if I have looked at the sun as it shone, or at the moon moving in splendor,
verses.31:27: and my heart was enticed in secret, and my hand kissed my mouth,
verses.31:28: that too would be an iniquity for judgment, for I would have denied God above.
verses.31:29: If I have rejoiced at the calamity of the one who hates me, or exulted when evil found him—
verses.31:30: no, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse.
verses.31:31: If the men of my tent have not said, "Who can find anyone who has not been filled with his meat?"—
verses.31:32: the sojourner did not lodge in the street; I opened my doors to the traveler.
verses.31:33: If I have concealed my transgressions like Adam, by hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
verses.31:34: because I dreaded the great multitude, and the contempt of the families terrified me, so that I kept silent and did not go out the door—
verses.31:35: If only I had someone to hear me! Here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me! And if only I had the document my adversary has written!
verses.31:36: Surely I would carry it upon my shoulder; I would tie it around myself as a crown.
verses.31:37: I would recount to Him the number of my steps; like a prince I would draw near to Him.
verses.31:38: If my ground has cried out against me, and its furrows have wept together,
verses.31:39: if I have eaten its yield without payment, or caused the life of its owners to expire,
verses.31:40: then let thorns spring up instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley. The words of Job are finished.
verses.32:1: Then these three men stopped answering Job, for he was righteous in his own eyes.
verses.32:2: And the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, burned. Against Job his anger burned because he declared himself righteous rather than God.
verses.32:3: And against his three friends his anger burned because they had found no answer, yet they had pronounced Job guilty.
verses.32:4: Now Elihu had waited for Job with words, for they were older than he in days.
verses.32:5: And Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger burned.
verses.32:6: Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, "I am young in days, and you are aged; therefore I shrank back and was afraid to declare my knowledge to you.
verses.32:7: I said, 'Days should speak, and an abundance of years should make wisdom known.'
verses.32:8: Yet truly, it is a spirit in a mortal, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
verses.32:9: It is not the great who become wise, nor do elders understand justice.
verses.32:10: Therefore I say, 'Listen to me; I also will declare my knowledge.'
verses.32:11: Look, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasonings while you searched out words.
verses.32:12: And I attended closely to you, and look, there was no one who refuted Job, none among you answering his sayings.
verses.32:13: Beware of saying, 'We have found wisdom; God will defeat him, not a man.'
verses.32:14: He has not arrayed words against me, and I will not reply to him with your sayings.
verses.32:15: They are dismayed; they do not answer any longer; words have departed from them.
verses.32:16: And should I wait because they do not speak, because they stand still and answer no more?
verses.32:17: I also will answer my part; I also will declare my knowledge.
verses.32:18: For I am full of words; the spirit in my belly presses me.
verses.32:19: Look, my belly is like wine that has not been opened; like new wineskins it is about to burst open.
verses.32:20: Let me speak so that relief may come to me; I will open my lips and answer.
verses.32:21: Let me show no partiality to any man, nor will I flatter any human.
verses.32:22: For I do not know how to flatter; my Maker would very soon carry me away."
verses.33:1: "However, please hear my speech, Job, and give ear to all my words.
verses.33:2: Look now, I have opened my mouth; my tongue speaks in my palate.
verses.33:3: My sayings are the uprightness of my heart, and my lips speak knowledge purely.
verses.33:4: The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty keeps me alive.
verses.33:5: If you are able, reply to me; array yourself before me; take your stand.
verses.33:6: Look, toward God I am just like you; from clay I too was pinched off.
verses.33:7: See, dread of me will not terrify you, and my pressure will not weigh heavy upon you.
verses.33:8: Indeed, you spoke in my ears, and I heard the sound of words:
verses.33:9: 'I am pure, with no transgression; I am clean, and I have no iniquity.
verses.33:10: Look, He finds pretexts against me; He regards me as an enemy to Himself.
verses.33:11: He places my feet in the stocks; He keeps watch over all my paths.'
verses.33:12: Look, in this you are not in the right; I will answer you, because God is greater than a mortal.
verses.33:13: Why have you contended against Him, that He does not answer for any of His matters?
verses.33:14: For in one way God speaks, and in two, yet no one perceives it.
verses.33:15: In a dream, a night vision, when deep sleep falls upon men, in slumbers upon a bed,
verses.33:16: then He uncovers the ear of men and seals their discipline,
verses.33:17: to turn a person aside from a deed, and to hide pride from a man.
verses.33:18: He holds back his soul from the pit, and his life from passing away by the weapon.
verses.33:19: Moreover, he is reproved with pain upon his bed, and in the multitude of his bones continually,
verses.33:20: so that his life causes him to abhor bread, and his soul desirable food.
